script: CHATGPT. DOESN'T. KNOW. SHIT. This happened tonight at midnight. I was on the night shift at a hotel in northern Italy, doing my usual grind when a guy strolls in with no reservation, asking for a walk‑in room. I was like, "Sure thing," and explained the 10‑euro deposit rule for walk‑ins, but suggested they book online to save cash. He had cash ready, but we don't accept cash for walk‑ins. We need a physical card to hold the deposit. He squinted at me, then said, "That's not what I read." I told him it was policy, written on our website. I pulled up the page, the rule was right there. He frowned, shook his head, and said, "No, that's not true. You must have added that just now. Here, this is what I know." He shoved his phone at my face, and a ChatGPT convo flashed: "Hotels in Italy don't require a credit card at check‑in." I took the deepest breath of my life. I already hate AI, I already hate entitled people, and I only have one more month before I can finally leave this job and keep my sanity. I explained that yes, we don't require a card if you've already paid online with a reservation. But for walk‑ins, the policy is clear. I pointed out the website from 2012, and how we're in the north, not the south. He kept pointing at the chat, insisting cash is accepted. I said, "Stop invading my space." I said, "ChatGPT pulls random data, not ours." I said, "If it was wrong, companies wouldn't be using it. You're just scared it'll do a better job than you." He demanded to speak to a manager. But wait — it gets worse. The manager had already gone home, but she'd said the same to anyone who'd come. I snapped, "ChatGPT is not an official source. Read the real website." He typed something new, shoved the phone again, and screamed, "You can't refuse service once you enter! See? It says it." I told him he wasn't a guest until he checked in or paid. I even cited two penal code articles, threatening police for trespassing and harassment. He left, hurling "fuck you," "this is a joke," and "you young people have no respect." The funniest was, "They created AI so people wouldn't have to deal with your Gen Z leftist propaganda." I laughed, but I could hear his voice echoing in the hallway. "Back in my day, you'd have been fired for that attitude." I thought, "If this didn't work, I'd lose everything." I walked back to the back office and cried for five minutes. The stress finally hit me like a punch. The night shift felt endless, and I still had to finish the job. I was left staring at the clock, wondering if I should actually call the police or just keep playing the role of the calm front‑desk warrior, because…
